title: Summer and Songbook
premise: June Calloway, a ghostwriter whose songs made other people famous, is stranded by a freak June snowstorm at Hollow Vineyards with Marcus Vane—the producer who stole credit for her breakout song a decade ago—and Dominic Sandoval, the vineyard owner who was her first love and first heartbreak. The storm traps all three for a week, forcing old wounds open: Marcus wants to buy the debt-ridden vineyard as a vanity estate, while June discovers Dominic has been quietly paying his workers' wages out of pocket since his father's death. As thaw comes, June must choose between signing with Marcus's label—the career that finally offers her visibility—or staying to help Dominic fight an unjust foreclosure through the town's informal network of neighbors, ledgers, and long memories. She chooses justice over the spotlight, exposes Marcus's stolen catalog at a harvest concert in the vineyard's ruined chapel, and builds a new life where belonging—not fame—is the song.
about_author: Ansel Halloran is the pen name of a former winery bookkeeper who spent fifteen years listening to stories over tasting-room counters before writing any of them down. They live in a valley that floods every spring and consider this a reasonable metaphor.

chapters.title: The Forecast Said Otherwise
chapters.summary: June's POV. En route to a career-saving meeting with producer Marcus Vane, June detours through her hometown valley and gets caught in an impossible June blizzard. She takes refuge at Hollow Vineyards, recognizing the name on the sign before she recognizes the man shoveling the drive. Beat: dread dressed up as coincidence.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Bad Timing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic Sandoval opens the door to find June Calloway, the girl who left him a note and a broken engagement twenty years ago, snowed onto his porch. He lets her in because he's not cruel, but he counts the hours until the roads clear. Beat: guarded hospitality masking old grief.

chapters.title: A Third Car in the Drift
chapters.summary: June's POV. A second stranded vehicle arrives: Marcus Vane himself, furious, charming, and carrying a contract in his briefcase. The three are stuck together, and June realizes Marcus doesn't recognize her—the ghostwriter he erased. Beat: the trap closes with polite laughter.

chapters.title: What the Vineyard Owes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Over forced dinner, Marcus probes the vineyard's finances and learns Dominic inherited debts instead of grapes—his father mortgaged everything to cover workers' medical bills. Dominic lies about how bad it is. Beat: pride as armor, and June noticing the lie.

chapters.title: Songs Nobody Signed
chapters.summary: June's POV. Snowbound evening turns to music; Dominic finds her old notebook in a box of returned belongings. He plays the melody of the song Marcus stole from her, from memory, after twenty years. Beat: being seen without permission—and wanting it anyway.

chapters.title: Marcus Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, sensing a bargain, offers to buy Hollow Vineyards at a predatory price, framing it as rescue. Privately he plans a vanity estate and a memoir rehabilitating his reputation. He also begins suspecting who June is. Beat: charm sharpening into threat.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: June's POV. Helping Dominic inventory the cellar, June finds his father's hidden ledger: decades of quiet debts paid to neighbors, favors owed both ways—a whole economy of justice outside banks and courts. Beat: understanding what kind of man raised the man she loved.

chapters.title: Thaw, Briefly
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Roads partially clear; Marcus leaves for the city to close financing, promising June a ride and a contract. Alone again, Dominic and June almost speak honestly about the breakup note—then don't. Beat: the near-miss that hurts more than a fight.

chapters.title: The Contract on the Table
chapters.summary: June's POV. In the city, Marcus offers June a headlining deal—if she signs away her back catalog, including the song he already stole. Her career, saved at last, requires becoming invisible again. Beat: ambition and self-betrayal shaking hands.

chapters.title: Foreclosure Notice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A certified letter: the bank, newly acquired by an investment group connected to Marcus, calls Dominic's loan due in ninety days. Legal channels are exhausted; his lawyer shrugs. Beat: the law revealing itself as just another power.

chapters.title: June Comes Back
chapters.summary: June's POV. Unable to sign, June returns to the valley unannounced, telling herself it's research. She finds the foreclosure notice on Dominic's kitchen table and, before thinking, starts reading it like a contract—which, professionally, she can do better than anyone. Beat: purpose arriving disguised as impulse.

chapters.title: The Town That Keeps Books
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. June and Dominic visit neighbors named in the old ledger: the feed-store owner, the retired judge, the choir director. Each owes or is owed something. An informal plan forms—buy the debt themselves, piece by piece, neighbor by neighbor. Beat: belonging as infrastructure.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Terms
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Raising money means asking for help, which means explaining why June left twenty years ago. At the grange hall, an old friend forces the question in front of her. June finally explains: she left because his father told her she'd bury her music in this valley. Beat: truth as excavation.

chapters.title: What His Father Knew
chapters.summary: June's POV. Reading the ledger's margins, June finds letters from Dominic's father to her—never sent—apologizing, urging her to go, taking the blame. Dominic learns his father sacrificed two loves to save one son. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Marcus Returns with Lawyers
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus arrives with the bank's attorneys and a press angle: rescuing a failing vineyard from itself. He also reveals he knows exactly who June is, and threatens to litigate her authorship claims into oblivion if she interferes. Beat: the villain showing his ledger too.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Spent Wisely
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Montage chapter: the town raises funds, June drafts a counter-offer using obscure agricultural-debt provisions, Dominic swallows pride and auctions his father's truck. Tension rises as they're still short, and Marcus tightens the timeline. Beat: hope under deadline.

chapters.title: The Stolen Song, Reclaimed
chapters.summary: June's POV. June uncovers proof—old studio session logs and a witness—that Marcus stole not just her song but others' work too. She must decide whether to use it publicly, knowing litigation could ruin her even if she wins. Beat: justice versus survival.

chapters.title: The Chapel Concert
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the foreclosure deadline eve, the town holds a benefit concert in the roofless chapel among the vines. June takes the stage for the first time under her own name and sings the stolen song, telling its true story between verses. Beat: climax—visibility chosen at last.

chapters.title: Where the Money Was
chapters.summary: June's POV. The concert goes viral locally; the retired judge produces evidence of the bank's improper loan practices; the investment group, fearing exposure, sells the debt to the neighbors' cooperative at par. Marcus retreats, his memoir deal collapsing. Beat: victory earned outside the courtroom.

chapters.title: The Contract She Doesn't Sign
chapters.summary: June's POV. Marcus, defeated but pragmatic, offers June one last clean deal—fame, touring, everything she wanted. She declines, choosing the valley, the co-op, and a small label run by the choir director's daughter. Beat: the choice made freely, not from fear.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Harvest begins with the whole town working the rows. Dominic finally asks June to stay—not as penance or nostalgia, but as a future. She answers by pinning a new song lyric to the cellar door, titled with his name. Beat: love as a decision renewed daily.

chapters.title: Summer and Songbook
chapters.summary: June's POV, epilogue. One year later: the vineyard solvent, the co-op thriving, June's first album under her own name recorded in the chapel. The final scene mirrors the first—a storm coming, three cars in the drive—but this time everyone stays by choice. Beat: belonging as the ending, and the beginning.
